`close`: Closes the element immediately.
`defer-otherwise-close`: Delegates the action to its parent component that has an
escape keydown handler. If no parent is found, it closes the element.
`defer-otherwise-ignore`: Delegates the action to the parent element. If no parent is found, nothing is done.
`ignore`: Prevents the element from closing and also blocks the parent element from closing in response to an escape key press.

entries.name: pagedNavigation
entries.description:
Applicable only when `numberOfMonths` is greater than 1.

Controls whether to use paged navigation for the next and previous buttons in the
date picker. With paged navigation set to `true`, clicking the next/prev buttons
changes all months in view. When set to `false`, it shifts the view by a single month.

For example, with `pagedNavigation` set to `true` and 2 months displayed (January and
February), clicking the next button changes the view to March and April. If `pagedNavigation`
is `false`, the view shifts to February and March.

should be formatted.

- "long": "Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", etc.
- "short": "Sun", "Mon", "Tue", etc.
- "narrow": "S", "M", "T", etc.

entries.name: isDateDisabled
entries.description:
A function that receives a date and returns `true` or `false` to indicate whether
the date is disabled.

entries.name: isDateUnavailable
entries.description:
Dates matching the provided matchers are marked as "unavailable." Unlike disabled dates,
users can still focus and select unavailable dates. However, selecting an unavailable date
renders the date picker as invalid.

For example, in a calendar for booking appointments, you might mark already booked dates as
unavailable. These dates could become available again before the appointment date, allowing
users to select them to learn more about the appointment.

`[data-unavailable]` - applied to unavailable dates

entries.name: fixedWeeks
entries.description:
Display 6 weeks per month, regardless the month's number of weeks.
This is useful for displaying a consistent calendar, where the size
of the calendar doesn't change month to month.

To display 6 weeks per month, you will need to render out the previous
and next month's dates in the calendar as well.

entries.name: numberOfMonths
entries.description:
Determines the number of months to display on the calendar simultaneously.
For navigation between months, refer to the `pagedNavigation` prop.

entries.name: calendarLabel
entries.description:
This label is exclusively used for accessibility, remaining hidden from the page.
It's read by screen readers when the calendar is opened. The current month and year
are automatically appended to the label, so you only need to provide the base label.

For instance:

entries.name: pagedNavigation
entries.description:
Applicable only when `numberOfMonths` is greater than 1.

Controls whether to use paged navigation for the next and previous buttons in the
date picker. With paged navigation set to `true`, clicking the next/prev buttons
changes all months in view. When set to `false`, it shifts the view by a single month.

For example, with `pagedNavigation` set to `true` and 2 months displayed (January and
February), clicking the next button changes the view to March and April. If `pagedNavigation`
is `false`, the view shifts to February and March.

entries.name: isDateUnavailable
entries.description:
Dates matching the provided matchers are marked as "unavailable." Unlike disabled dates,
users can still focus and select unavailable dates. However, selecting an unavailable date
renders the date picker as invalid.

For example, in a calendar for booking appointments, you might mark already booked dates as
unavailable. These dates could become available again before the appointment date, allowing
users to select them to learn more about the appointment.

`[data-unavailable]` - applied to unavailable dates

entries.name: fixedWeeks
entries.description:
Display 6 weeks per month, regardless the month's number of weeks.
This is useful for displaying a consistent calendar, where the size
of the calendar doesn't change month to month.

To display 6 weeks per month, you will need to render out the previous
and next month's dates in the calendar as well.

entries.name: numberOfMonths

entries.name: calendarLabel
entries.description:
This label is exclusively used for accessibility, remaining hidden from the page.
It's read by screen readers when the calendar is opened. The current month and year
are automatically appended to the label, so you only need to provide the base label.

For instance:
- 'Date of birth' will be read as 'Date of birth, January 2021' if the current month is January 2021.
- 'Appointment date' will be read as 'Appointment date, January 2021' if the current month is January 2021.
- 'Booking date' will be read as 'Booking date, January 2021' if the current month is January 2021.

entries.name: aria-activedescendant
entries.description: Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox, group, or application.

entries.name: aria-atomic
entries.description: Indicates whether assistive technologies will present all, or only parts of, the changed region based on the change notifications defined by the aria-relevant attribute.

entries.name: aria-autocomplete
entries.description:
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be
presented if they are made.

entries.name: aria-busy
entries.description: Indicates an element is being modified and that assistive technologies MAY want to wait until the modifications are complete before exposing them to the user.

entries.name: aria-checked
entries.description: Indicates the current "checked" state of checkboxes, radio buttons, and other widgets.

entries.name: aria-colcount
entries.description: Defines the total number of columns in a table, grid, or treegrid.

entries.name: aria-colindex
entries.description: Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid.

entries.name: aria-colspan
entries.description: Defines the number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

entries.name: aria-controls
entries.description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

entries.name: aria-current
entries.description: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

entries.name: aria-describedby
entries.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

entries.name: aria-details
entries.description: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

entries.name: aria-disabled
entries.description: Indicates that the element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable.

entries.name: aria-dropeffect
entries.description: Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target.

entries.name: aria-errormessage
entries.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

entries.name: aria-expanded
entries.description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

entries.name: aria-flowto
entries.description:
Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion,
allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

entries.name: aria-grabbed
entries.description: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation.

entries.name: aria-haspopup
entries.description: Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.

entries.name: aria-hidden
entries.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

entries.name: aria-invalid
entries.description: Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

entries.name: aria-keyshortcuts
entries.description: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

entries.name: aria-label
entries.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

entries.name: aria-labelledby
entries.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

entries.name: aria-level
entries.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

entries.name: aria-live
entries.description: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

entries.name: aria-modal
entries.description: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

entries.name: aria-multiline
entries.description: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

entries.name: aria-multiselectable
entries.description: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

entries.name: aria-orientation
entries.description: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

entries.name: aria-owns
entries.description:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

entries.name: aria-placeholder
entries.description:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

entries.name: aria-posinset
entries.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

entries.name: aria-pressed
entries.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

entries.name: aria-readonly
entries.description: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

entries.name: aria-relevant
entries.type: "text" | "additions" | "additions removals" | "additions text" | "all" | "removals" | "removals additions" | "removals text" | "text additions" | "text removals" | null | undefined
entries.description: Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.

entries.name: aria-required
entries.description: Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

entries.name: aria-roledescription
entries.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

entries.name: aria-rowcount
entries.description: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.

entries.name: aria-rowindex
entries.description: Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

entries.name: aria-rowspan
entries.description: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

entries.name: aria-selected
entries.description: Indicates the current "selected" state of various widgets.

entries.name: aria-setsize
entries.description: Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

entries.name: aria-sort
entries.description: Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.

entries.name: aria-valuemax
entries.description: Defines the maximum allowed value for a range widget.

entries.name: aria-valuemin
entries.description: Defines the minimum allowed value for a range widget.

entries.name: aria-valuenow

Interact outside behavior type.
`close`: Closes the element immediately.
`defer-otherwise-close`: Delegates the action to the parent element. If no parent is found, it closes the element.
`defer-otherwise-ignore`: Delegates the action to the parent element. If no parent is found, nothing is done.
`ignore`: Prevents the element from closing and also blocks the parent element from closing in response to an outside interaction.

entries.name: escapeKeydownBehavior
entries.description:
Escape behavior type.
`close`: Closes the element immediately.
`defer-otherwise-close`: Delegates the action to its parent component that has an
escape keydown handler. If no parent is found, it closes the element.
`defer-otherwise-ignore`: Delegates the action to the parent element. If no parent is found, nothing is done.
`ignore`: Prevents the element from closing and also blocks the parent element from closing in response to an escape key press.
